findings.title: Required descriptor capabilities failed open
findings.reproduction_detail: With O_PATH/O_NOFOLLOW/dir_fd support disabled and manifest.json made a symlink to a file outside the bundle, read_bundle_file returned OK and read the external bytes via the full-path fallback.
findings.disposition_detail: descriptor_primitives_available() gates the read; a missing O_NOFOLLOW/O_PATH/O_NONBLOCK/dir_fd yields UNSUPPORTED and validate_bundle fails the whole gate closed with BUNDLE_DESCRIPTOR_UNSUPPORTED before reading any bundle bytes. No pathname-check-then-open substitute. Capability matrix (drop each primitive and combinations, against manifest/final/intermediate external symlinks) proves external bytes are never read.

findings.title: cap-plus-one memory claim was false
findings.reproduction_detail: _read_fd_capped accumulated a chunk list then joined; both coexist during join. A 4 MiB read peaked at ~8 MiB via tracemalloc; a 64 MiB cap would peak ~128 MiB.
findings.disposition_detail: One growing bytearray, returned as a bytes-like object; no chunk list, no whole-payload join. tracemalloc peak measured ~1.25x payload (payload plus one read chunk) versus ~2x. Post-fstat growth and short reads preserved. Every 'never buffers more than cap+1' statement corrected in code comments, contract doc, this JSON, the Markdown audit, and HANDOFF.md.

findings.title: Mutable verified-byte identity: evaluator could receive bytes whose digest no longer matched
findings.reproduction_detail: _read_fd_capped returned a bytearray; check_integrity hashed it, then aliased the SAME mutable object into both verified_bytes and raw_bytes; evaluate_semantics sent that object to the evaluator without re-proving the digest. Reproduced through the real gate on a copy of the reference bundle: a hook on the stage immediately before semantic evaluation flipped one JSON-insignificant space (0x20) to a tab (0x09) in verified_bytes in place; the gate returned ok=True and the bridge received bytes whose SHA-256 (8f99..., cc71...) differed from both the observed digest and the manifest digests (f16a..., ffab...).
findings.disposition_detail: At the point the digest promise is made (digest match in check_integrity), the verified bytes are frozen into an immutable bytes object (frozen = bytes(raw); del raw) and both verified_bytes and raw_bytes reference that single immutable object. An immutable bytes object cannot be mutated in place by any alias, so the bytes parsed, schema-checked, and evaluated are byte-for-byte the ones integrity bound. Re-running the reproduction through the real gate: verified_bytes is now bytes, the in-place mutation is refused ('bytes' object does not support item assignment), and the evaluator receives bytes whose SHA-256 equals the manifest digests.
findings.memory_reconciliation: The freeze is a deliberate, one-time, per-artifact second payload-sized allocation: the bytearray and its bytes copy coexist for the duration of the copy, then the bytearray is released. This does NOT reinstate the round-2 chunk-list double-peak: the bounded reader still owns a single buffer and makes no whole-payload copy (that property is scoped to the reader). The 'no whole-payload copy' claim is corrected in the reader docstring, the contract doc, and this record to be reader-scoped, not whole-lifecycle, and the freeze copy is disclosed.
findings.regression_and_mutation_evidence: Public-gate regressions added: test_verified_bytes_are_frozen_immutable_after_integrity (verified_bytes/raw_bytes are the same immutable bytes object; in-place assignment raises), test_evaluator_receives_bytes_matching_the_manifest_digest (bridge boundary instrumented; every payload sent hashes to a declared manifest digest), test_pre_semantic_mutation_cannot_alter_the_evaluated_subject (the reproduction, as a regression: the in-place whitespace flip is refused and the evaluator still receives digest-matching bytes). A mutation removing the freeze (restoring the bytearray alias) is killed by these tests: the mutation attempt succeeds and the evaluator receives non-matching bytes.

findings.title: Capability matrix did not prove no read (vacuous secret[:0] assertion)
findings.reproduction_detail: The capability-matrix tests only asserted the external secret text was absent from GateResult, and one term (secret[:0]) checked zero secret bytes, so it was vacuous. Absence from the rendered result does not prove the external bytes were never opened or read.
findings.disposition_detail: The 15-case capability matrix (manifest, final-, and intermediate-component external symlink x each dropped primitive and the combined case) now instruments the gate's real os.open/os.read boundary and asserts zero opens and zero reads after the capability preflight fails. A control test (test_open_read_instrumentation_observes_reads_and_preserves_detection) proves the spies leave descriptor_primitives_available() intact when primitives are present and actually observe a real open and read, so a zero count in the matrix is a genuine no-access, not a broken detector. The instrumentation preserves the dir_fd view (registers the spy in supports_dir_fd when dir_fd is meant to be supported) so the preflight fails only because of the dropped O_* flag, never because os.open was replaced.
